item.title: Physicist develops detector capable of counting photons for quantum computing
item.description: Detecting a single photon is a challenge in itself. But what if you also want to know exactly how many photons arrive at a particular point at the same time? Physicist Erik Baalbergen is working on light detectors that can do just that. They form a key building block for the optical quantum computer of the future.

item.title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing
Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum algorithms for elastic media simulation have been conjectured to offer up to a quartic quantum advantage over classical methods; however, the devil is always in the details. Here, we determine key physical conditions under which this quartic separation could be achieved in the relevant parameters. For continuum elastic dynamics at fixed volume with spatial convergence order $m$, we find that the end-to-end speedup is of order $(m+4)/(m+1)$

item.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
All Bell inequalities with a quantum advantage in the minimal scenario are self-testing
item.description: arXiv:2611.06997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the minimal Bell scenario, all extremal quantum correlations are known, but the Tsirelson inequalities that delimit the quantum set remain poorly understood. We study which correlations can maximize a given Tsirelson inequality, and conversely, which inequalities are maximized by a given correlation.
